coverage_summary: Most Stage 1 AR data-flow steps are supported, including pseudo-bulk preparation, BioFM encoding, projection, tokenization, lookup, injection, and teacher-forced training. The target lookup asserts an unsupported table identity.

findings.detail: The target-text lookup reuses query_embedding_table, asserting that query and target text use the same materialized embedding-table resource. The paper states that AR consumes Tokens(t_b), while target-language representations may be constructed through several target-embedding choices; the graph itself records this sharing as uncertain.

evidence.quote: When performing alignment training using AR loss, the model consumes Tokens ( t b ) directly, since the objective is next-token prediction over a text sequence.

We evaluate four ways to construct ϕ ( t ) : (1) TokEmbed , averaging input embeddings; (2) LL-Mean , mean pooling of the final layer; (3) LayerAvg , averaging several top layers; and (4) LLM-Embed , a co-trained text encoder when available.

findings.required_change: Remove the asserted reuse of query_embedding_table for embed_target. Use a target-specific implicit table/resource with sharing left unspecified, or retain the target-text embedding path as an opaque boundary.

findings.detail: The parameter value “Granite tokenizer, unspecified” is more specific than the cited text, which establishes tokenization but does not identify the tokenizer implementation.

evidence.quote: Here, Tokens ( · ) denotes text after tokenization and embedding lookup.

findings.required_change: Change the vocabulary parameter to “LLM tokenizer, unspecified” unless the paper explicitly names the Granite tokenizer.
